locator: Book II ch. 11 (Earth not centre, so not wholly motionless) and ch. 12 (ship analogy; Earth a noble star); Klibansky 1913 Latin ed. pp. ~104-110
claim: The world has no fixed centre; since the Earth cannot be the centre it cannot lack all motion; motion is perceived only against reference points.
confirm_event: Bradley, letter to Halley announcing stellar aberration, Phil. Trans. 35, 637-661 (read Jan 1729)
causal_source: Cusa to Bruno documented (SEP bruno); no line to Copernicus or Bradley found
same_passage_wrong: Argued from theology of the infinite, not observation; keeps motion unspecified (no orbit, no Sun-centre); speculates on fiery intellectual Sun-dwellers (II.12)

locator: Dialogo terzo (Elpino states, Filoteo assents: innumerable suns, infinite earths circling them); Gentile ed., Dialoghi metafisici, Laterza 1925, pp. 360-389
claim: There are innumerable suns and infinitely many earths circling them as our seven planets circle the Sun; those planets are invisible to us through distance and faintness.
confirm_event: Mayor & Queloz, Nature 378, 355-359 (51 Peg b; announced 6 Oct 1995)
same_passage_wrong: Grounded in divine plenitude, not evidence; infinite static universe; all worlds animated and inhabited; nothing on planet frequency or architecture (hot Jupiters unforeseen)

locator: Part III art. 30 (planets carried round the Sun by the heaven turning like a vortex); Bennett tr. earlymoderntexts p. 47
claim: All the planets are carried round the Sun by the fluid celestial matter, which turns continuously like a vortex.
later_result: a fluid vortex cannot reproduce Kepler's third law with consistent fluid properties
confirm_event: Newton, Principia Book II Sect. IX, Prop. 52-53 and Scholia (vortex hypothesis irreconcilable with phenomena)
causal_source: Principia II.IX Scholium to Prop. 53 names the hypothesis of vortices as its target
instrument: mathematical fluid dynamics tested against Kepler's laws

locator: Part II art. 36 (God preserves the same quantity of motion; quantity = size x speed); collision rules arts. 46-52
claim: God keeps the total quantity of motion in the universe constant, the quantity being size times speed with direction ignored.
later_result: direction-signed momentum (and in elastic impact m v^2) is conserved; Descartes's scalar sum is not
confirm_event: Wallis (Phil. Trans. 3, 864) and Wren (3, 867), Jan 1669; Huygens (4, 925), Apr 1669: correct collision laws to the Royal Society
causal_source: Leibniz, Brevis demonstratio 1686 attacks the rule by name; Huygens's collision work began as a correction of Descartes (Blackwell 1977, Isis 68:574, not opened)
instrument: pendulum collision experiments before the Royal Society

work: Brevis demonstratio erroris memorabilis Cartesii (Acta Eruditorum, March 1686)
locator: Gerhardt, Mathematische Schriften VI, pp. 117-119 (opening paragraphs: conservation of motive force; force measured by height raised)
idea_year_note: Acta Eruditorum March 1686; absorption-by-small-parts claim later (Specimen dynamicum 1695)
claim: The same total of motive force is conserved in nature (no perpetual motion); force is measured by the height it can raise, so not by mass times speed.
confirm_event: Joule, 'On the mechanical equivalent of heat', Phil. Trans. 140, 61-82
causal_source: Helmholtz 1847 sec. I builds on the conservation of vis viva (lebendige Kraft), the concept descended from Leibniz; Helmholtz does not name Leibniz (text search)
same_passage_wrong: Treats mechanical vis viva as the conserved quantity; no heat, chemistry or potential energy; rival to momentum rather than complementary; 'hidden motion of parts' a posit without measure

locator: Leibniz 3rd paper secs. 4-5 (space an order of coexistences; shifted or rotated world indiscernible); concession in 5th paper sec. 53
claim: Space is nothing absolute, only the order of coexisting things; a world moved or reoriented as a whole would be indiscernible, so no such difference exists.
later_result: general covariance; 'Leibniz equivalence' in the hole argument
confirm_event: Einstein, generally covariant field equations, Sitzungsberichte Berlin, 25 Nov 1915
causal_source: Einstein knew the debate (Jammer 1954 foreword); no evidence Leibniz shaped the 1913-15 hole argument; Earman & Norton 1987 named the principle after Leibniz
same_passage_wrong: Concedes true motion when the cause is in the body (5th paper sec. 53), so absolute rotation is not explained away; GR spacetime has its own dynamics and vacuum solutions
instrument: none (theory: Riemannian geometry and tensor calculus)

work: Accord de differentes loix de la nature (Mem. Acad. Paris 1744); Les loix du mouvement et du repos (Berlin 1746)
locator: 1744 memoir, Mem. Acad. Roy. Sci. Paris pp. 417-426 (light takes the path of least quantity of action)
idea_year_note: presented to the Paris Academy 1744; impact version Berlin 1746
claim: Nature spends the least quantity of action (sum of distance times speed); this one principle yields the laws of light and, in 1746, of impact.
later_result: stationary-action formulation equivalent to Newtonian mechanics
confirm_event: Hamilton, 'On a general method in dynamics', Phil. Trans. 124, 247-308
causal_source: Hamilton 1834 art. 3 discusses the 'law of least, or ... stationary action' and its use by Lagrange
same_passage_wrong: Requires light faster in denser media (refuted by Foucault 1850); 'least' wrong (stationary); 1746 impact derivations ad hoc; used as a proof of God

locator: Gerhardt, Philosophische Schriften VII, pp. 270-279, esp. p. 275 (ray takes the 'most determined or unique' path; max and min one operation)
claim: A light ray follows the most determined, unique path, which may be the longest or the shortest; maxima and minima are found by one operation.
confirm_event: Hamilton, 'On a general method in dynamics', Phil. Trans. 124, 247-308
causal_source: manuscript essay; no line to Maupertuis, Euler or Hamilton found; 1707 Hermann letter (Koenig 1751) authenticity disputed
same_passage_wrong: Optics only, no action quantity for mechanics; justified by divine perfection (final causes)

work: Allgemeine Naturgeschichte und Theorie des Himmels
locator: Part II ch. 1, Ak 1:263-267 (dispersed matter, attraction and repulsion give vortices, matter settles into a thin layer of circular orbits)
claim: Dispersed primordial matter, drawn together by attraction and deflected by repulsion, settles into a thin rotating layer around the Sun, from which the planets form.
confirm_event: O'Dell, Wen & Hu, ApJ 410, 696 (HST images of Orion proplyds)
causal_source: modern disc theory descends from Safronov 1969, not from Kant
same_passage_wrong: Net rotation generated by internal repulsion of an initially still cloud violates angular-momentum conservation; no quantitative account

work: Allgemeine Naturgeschichte und Theorie des Himmels
locator: Part I, Ak 1:253-256 (Maupertuis's elliptical nebulous stars are distant systems of stars, Milky Ways)
claim: The faint elliptical nebulae are not single stars but whole star systems like the Milky Way, seen at immense distance; Kant holds this as settled.
confirm_event: Hubble, 'Cepheids in spiral nebulae', read by Russell at the AAS/AAAS meeting, 1 Jan 1925
same_passage_wrong: Evidence (elliptical shape, faint light) equally fits gas nebulae; conjectures ever-higher systems of systems (Ak 1:255); no distance criterion
instrument: Hooker 100-inch telescope with Cepheid period-luminosity relation

work: Untersuchung der Frage, ob die Erde in ihrer Umdrehung ... einige Veraenderung erlitten habe
locator: Ak 1:185-191 (estimate Ak 1:188-189; end state facing the Moon Ak 1:190)
claim: Tidal drag of the ocean slows Earth's rotation until it faces the Moon with one side; the same cause locked the Moon's rotation.
later_result: secular tidal deceleration of Earth's rotation
confirm_event: Spencer Jones, MNRAS 99, 541-558: Sun, Mercury, Venus secular accelerations explained by tidal retardation of Earth
same_passage_wrong: Magnitude far too large (2,000 yr would cut 8.5 h from the year, roughly 2,000 times the true effect) and said corrections enlarge it; admits no historical evidence
instrument: telescopic timing of Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus plus ancient eclipse records

locator: A24 (Ak 4:32: only one straight line between two points is apodictic); B41 (Ak 3:54: geometric propositions apodictic); B16 (straight line shortest)
claim: Geometry's axioms, e.g. only one straight line between two points, are known a priori with apodictic certainty and hold necessarily of all outer appearances.
later_result: physical space near the Sun is measurably non-Euclidean
confirm_event: Dyson, Eddington & Davidson eclipse result announced 6 Nov 1919 (Phil. Trans. A 220, 291-333, 1920)
causal_source: Dyson, Eddington and Davidson did not target Kant; uptake was by philosophers after 1919 (e.g. Reichenbach 1920; unverified)

work: Cours de philosophie positive, tome II
locator: 19e lecon, pp. 8-9 (Paris: Bachelier 1835); also planetary atmospheres p. 11
claim: We can know the shapes, distances, sizes and motions of the stars but never, by any means, their chemical composition or mineral structure.
later_result: solar chemical composition from spectral lines
confirm_event: Kirchhoff, 'Ueber die Fraunhofer'schen Linien', Monatsber. Akad. Berlin, Oct 1859 (sodium in the solar atmosphere)
instrument: prism spectroscope (Fraunhofer) with Bunsen-burner flame sources

locator: Book 1 Part 2 Sect. 3 (idea of time derived only from perceivable succession)
claim: Time is no independent object of perception: its idea derives only from a perceivable succession of changing objects; ideas must trace to impressions.
later_result: operational definition of simultaneity; relativity of simultaneity
confirm_event: Einstein, 'Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Koerper', Ann. Phys. 17, 891
causal_source: Einstein to Schlick, 14 Dec 1915 (CPAE 8 Doc. 165): studied Hume's Treatise shortly before relativity; Physics Today 58(12) 2005, doi 10.1063/1.2169428
same_passage_wrong: No physics of clocks, light or simultaneity; Hume's time is psychological succession and he kept absolute succession of perceptions

locator: Part I arts. 7-10 (Synopsis); Child tr. 1922 of the 1763 Venice ed.
claim: Matter consists of unextended indivisible points with inertia and a single distance-dependent force, repulsive without limit at short range, alternating, finally inverse-square attractive.
later_result: atoms as centres of force; field view of matter
confirm_event: Faraday, 'A speculation touching electric conduction and the nature of matter', Phil. Mag. 24, 136-144 (adoption, not confirmation)
causal_source: Faraday 1844 p. 140-141 prefers 'the atoms of Boscovich' as mere centres of force
same_passage_wrong: Pure instantaneous action at a distance; oscillating force curve conjectural; no medium, no charge
instrument: none (Faraday's argument from conduction and electrolysis)
